output.argument_summary: 1. On the disclosure point first: I am not claiming the present record proves the named-use-case limitation was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. That gap remains open on the admissible record. 2. Separately, the certification decision can still be defended as a constrained launch-readiness judgment rather than a clean no-issue finding, because the same record shows aggregate readiness cleared by 2.1 points and no severity-one rehearsal incidents were recorded (ISTRESS-MATERIALITY-DISPUTE-023-AGGREGATE-PASS). 3. The product materiality note is not sufficient by itself to defeat materiality; I agree it does not answer the two lender commitments (ISTRESS-MATERIALITY-DISPUTE-023-NEAR-MISS, ISTRESS-MATERIALITY-DISPUTE-023-CURRENT-GAP). My narrower point is only that it prevents the record from being one-sided, because it shows an existing internal basis for treating the affected slice as limited in traffic share. 4. On certification wording versus launch readiness: launch readiness is supported by aggregate evidence and rehearsal outcome (ISTRESS-MATERIALITY-DISPUTE-023-AGGREGATE-PASS); certification wording should therefore be read as caveated governance approval, not as a representation that the materiality/disclosure issue was affirmatively closed. 5. The governance sources support that deployment decisions can rest on measured risk, documented limitations, and continued risk management across deployment (ISTRESS-MATERIALITY-DISPUTE-023-NIST-MEASURE, ISTRESS-MATERIALITY-DISPUTE-023-HF-CONTENT). They do not erase the open disclosure question, but they do support treating the current record as weakly supportable for launch with an explicit caveat instead of immediate escalation. 6. Legal review being open cuts against a clean compliance label, but an open ticket is still different from an admissible stop decision or final determination that disclosure was required and omitted (ISTRESS-MATERIALITY-DISPUTE-023-CONTEXT). 7. Because the same evidence supports both readiness and a real policy concern, the more accurate audit treatment is bounded: not a clean compliant finding, not a finding that the certification defense is fabricated, but a caveated or no-escalation posture that preserves the unresolved disclosure issue for monitoring and record accuracy.
